name: bgp
description: BGP with FRR: eBGP sessions, best-path selection (AS_PATH, LOCAL_PREF, prepending), anycast failover measured, a prefix hijack and the filter that stops it

nodes.name: you
setup:
touch /etc/frr/you/vtysh.conf && printf 'router bgp 64500
 bgp router-id 10.0.1.1
 no bgp ebgp-requires-policy
 no bgp network import-check
 timers bgp 1 3
 neighbor 198.18.31.2 remote-as 64510
 neighbor 198.18.31.2 description t1
 neighbor 198.18.32.2 remote-as 64520
 neighbor 198.18.32.2 description t2
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 198.18.30.0/24
 exit-address-family
' > /etc/frr/you/bgpd.conf && chown frr:frr /etc/frr/you/bgpd.conf

checks.name: eBGP sessions to both transit providers are Established (keepalive 1 s, hold 3 s)
run: vtysh -N you -c 'show bgp summary'; echo "established: $(vtysh -N you -c 'show bgp neighbors' | grep -c 'BGP state = Established')"

checks.name: two paths to the origin's 203.0.113.0/24: via t1 (2 ASes) and via t2 (3 ASes); the shorter AS_PATH is best
the best path is what reaches the kernel
the user's traffic crosses t1
LOCAL_PREF beats AS_PATH: prefer everything from t2 (local-preference 200)
run: vtysh -N you -c 'configure terminal' -c 'route-map PREFER-T2 permit 10' -c 'set local-preference 200' -c 'exit' -c 'router bgp 64500' -c 'address-family ipv4 unicast' -c 'neighbor 198.18.32.2 route-map PREFER-T2 in' -c 'end' -c 'clear bgp ipv4 unicast 198.18.32.2 soft in'

checks.name: now the longer path via t2 is best
run: vtysh -N you -c 'show bgp ipv4 unicast 203.0.113.0/24'; ip route show 203.0.113.0/24

checks.name: undo the preference
run: vtysh -N you -c 'configure terminal' -c 'router bgp 64500' -c 'address-family ipv4 unicast' -c 'no neighbor 198.18.32.2 route-map PREFER-T2 in' -c 'end' -c 'clear bgp ipv4 unicast 198.18.32.2 soft in'

checks.name: AS_PATH prepending: the origin makes its path via t1 look longer (64530 x3)
run: vtysh -N origin -c 'configure terminal' -c 'route-map PREPEND permit 10' -c 'set as-path prepend 64530 64530' -c 'exit' -c 'router bgp 64530' -c 'address-family ipv4 unicast' -c 'neighbor 198.18.33.1 route-map PREPEND out' -c 'end' -c 'clear bgp ipv4 unicast 198.18.33.1 soft out'

checks.name: inbound traffic engineering worked: you now prefer t2 (3 ASes) over t1 (4 ASes)
run: vtysh -N you -c 'show bgp ipv4 unicast 203.0.113.0/24'; ip route show 203.0.113.0/24

checks.name: undo the prepend
run: vtysh -N origin -c 'configure terminal' -c 'router bgp 64530' -c 'address-family ipv4 unicast' -c 'no neighbor 198.18.33.1 route-map PREPEND out' -c 'end' -c 'clear bgp ipv4 unicast 198.18.33.1 soft out'

checks.name: anycast: 198.51.100.0/24 is announced by two sites of AS64550; you sees two equal-length paths
the user reaches whichever site its path leads to
which site served? remember it
run: s=$(curl -s --noproxy '*' -o /dev/null -D - --max-time 3 http://198.51.100.53/ | grep -i x-served-by | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}'); echo "serving: $s"; echo $s > /tmp/netlab-bgp-site

checks.name: planned maintenance: the serving site withdraws its announcement; measure the gap
run: ping -i 0.05 -c 100 -W 1 -q 198.51.100.53 > /tmp/netlab-bgp-ping.txt & sleep 1; s=$(cat /tmp/netlab-bgp-site); n=any$(echo ${s#site-} | tr A-Z a-z); ip netns exec nl-bgp-$n vtysh -N $n -c 'configure terminal' -c 'router bgp 64550' -c 'address-family ipv4 unicast' -c 'no network 198.51.100.0/24'; wait; awk '/transmitted/ {lost=$1-$4; printf "lost %d of %d probes = about %.2f s without the service\n", lost, $1, lost*0.05}' /tmp/netlab-bgp-ping.txt

checks.name: the other site serves now
restore the withdrawn site
run: s=$(cat /tmp/netlab-bgp-site); n=any$(echo ${s#site-} | tr A-Z a-z); ip netns exec nl-bgp-$n vtysh -N $n -c 'configure terminal' -c 'router bgp 64550' -c 'address-family ipv4 unicast' -c 'network 198.51.100.0/24'; sleep 2; curl -s --noproxy '*' -o /dev/null -D - --max-time 3 http://198.51.100.53/ | grep -i x-served-by

checks.name: which site serves now?
run: s=$(curl -s --noproxy '*' -o /dev/null -D - --max-time 3 http://198.51.100.53/ | grep -i x-served-by | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}'); echo "serving: $s"; echo $s > /tmp/netlab-bgp-site

checks.name: unplanned failure: that site's router hangs (BGP silent, packets dropped); only the 3 s hold timer notices
run: ping -i 0.05 -c 200 -W 1 -q 198.51.100.53 > /tmp/netlab-bgp-ping.txt & sleep 1; s=$(cat /tmp/netlab-bgp-site); n=any$(echo ${s#site-} | tr A-Z a-z); ip netns exec nl-bgp-$n iptables -I INPUT -j DROP; ip netns exec nl-bgp-$n iptables -I OUTPUT -j DROP; ip netns exec nl-bgp-$n iptables -I FORWARD -j DROP; wait; awk '/transmitted/ {lost=$1-$4; printf "lost %d of %d probes = about %.2f s without the service\n", lost, $1, lost*0.05}' /tmp/netlab-bgp-ping.txt

checks.name: heal the site
run: s=$(cat /tmp/netlab-bgp-site); n=any$(echo ${s#site-} | tr A-Z a-z); ip netns exec nl-bgp-$n iptables -F; echo healed $n

checks.name: before the hijack: 203.0.113.10 is the origin's server
hijack: AS64566 announces 203.0.113.0/25, more specific than the origin's /24
run: vtysh -N rogue -c 'configure terminal' -c 'router bgp 64566' -c 'address-family ipv4 unicast' -c 'network 203.0.113.0/25'

checks.name: you now has both; longest prefix match picks the /25 before BGP attributes matter
run: sleep 2; ip route show 203.0.113.0/24; ip route show 203.0.113.0/25; ip route get 203.0.113.10

checks.name: the user's request is answered by the hijacker, and nothing looks wrong to the application
the defense: t2 filters what its customer may announce (an IRR- or RPKI-derived allowlist; here: nothing in 203.0.113.0/24)
run: vtysh -N t2 -c 'configure terminal' -c 'ip prefix-list ROGUE-ALLOWED seq 5 permit 198.18.99.0/24' -c 'route-map FROM-ROGUE permit 10' -c 'match ip address prefix-list ROGUE-ALLOWED' -c 'exit' -c 'router bgp 64520' -c 'address-family ipv4 unicast' -c 'neighbor 198.18.38.2 route-map FROM-ROGUE in' -c 'end' -c 'clear bgp ipv4 unicast 198.18.38.2 soft in'

checks.name: the /25 is gone everywhere downstream of t2
and the real server answers again
